chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyam, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Hajj and did not touch (kiss) the Stone, so he said: 'It is from the Sunnah; if he is unable to do so, then Allah is more deserving of making excuses.'
ai.seo_question: Is touching the Black Stone obligatory during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that Istilam (touching the Black Stone) is a confirmed Sunnah rather than a fundamental pillar of Hajj, emphasizing the principle of ease in worship. The Imam’s statement that 'Allah is more deserving of excuse' underscores the Shia scholarly view that physical incapacity or difficulty fully absolves the pilgrim, reflecting the broader juristic consensus on removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) in ritual acts.
